title: Small diagnostic benchmark
cells_executed: command-line task, no notebook. Learner personally ran: the offline tests, benchmark runs fp32-a and fp32-b (identical settings), the check-repro comparison, the bfloat16 parameter-change run, the Task 08 device-row import, and a self-initiated json64 follow-up run (--only json_med --gen-tokens 64) to test the JSON-truncation hypothesis.

runs.fp32-a: 24 rows, pytorch_local float32, 8 prompts x 3 reps
runs.qdc-774303: 2 rows imported from Task 08 geniex-bench medians, w4a16 on Snapdragon 8 Elite, both stamped unlike_runtime_warning

parameters_changed.result: bfloat16 was about 1.7x faster (decode 31.7 -> 54.8 tok/s short, 22.1 -> 33.6 long; TTFT lower) and every output_sha256 matched float32 on all 8 prompts: no greedy argmax flip in this sample. Peak RSS last row 0.67 GB (bf16) vs 2.04 GB (fp32).
parameters_changed.extra_change: gen tokens 48 -> 64 on json_med (learner-initiated json64 run)

findings: Reproducibility PASS: all 24 output hashes identical between fp32-a and fp32-b; timings within about 1%.

TTFT grows with prompt length but sublinearly: 19x more prompt tokens cost 6.6x more time. prefill_tps climbs from 494 to about 1480 tok/s and saturates near P=500 (fixed per-pass launch overhead dominates short prompts).

Decode slows with real cache length: 31.7 tok/s at P=27 down to 22.1 at P=525. Refines the Task 08 finding: the phone varied only the allocated context (-c) with a fixed 128-token prompt, so no change appeared; decode cost follows actual KV length, not the configured maximum. Flagged for Task 10.

json_valid was False on both JSON prompts at the 48-token cap; both hit the cap exactly while inst_short stopped on EOS at 41. The json64 run proved the truncation hypothesis: at cap 64 the model finished at 56 tokens with json_valid true in all 3 reps.
Deployment-gain observation (unlike runtime paths, warning attached): device w4a16 decode 108 tok/s and prefill 6480 tok/s vs local float32 22-32 tok/s decode and about 1500 tok/s prefill.
No output failures; decode spread tight within runs, so no visible thermal throttling.

review_evidence.tests: uv run pytest tests/test_task09_bench.py -q: 10 passed at review time (37 passed repo-wide)
review_evidence.check_repro: uv run python -m edge_slm_lab.diag_bench --check-repro fp32-a fp32-b: tokens SAME on all 24 pairs, reproducibility: PASS, exit 0
review_evidence.row_audit: 77 rows; fp32-a/fp32-b/bf16 each cover all 8 prompt ids x 3 reps; both device rows carry unlike_runtime_warning
review_evidence.secret_scan: check_text clean on the whole JSONL (enforced per line at write time, re-run at review)
